title: Safe patch and firmware rotation playbook for private deployments
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines a safe, repeatable process for performing host OS patches, accelerator firmware updates, and associated runtime library rotations for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It is intended for field operators and SREs responsible for day‑2 maintenance where the goal is to apply security and firmware updates with minimal customer impact and clear forensic evidence in case of rollbacks.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to private deployments that run the Redwood runtime on customer-managed infrastructure (VPC leases or on‑prem racks).
- Covers node-level OS package upgrades, GPU/accelerator firmware upgrades, and model-serving runtime library (inference engine) swaps that require coordinated node restarts.
- Not intended for control-plane-only control updates; see operator control-plane swap guides for those procedures.

Owner and roles:
- Owner: Private Deployments Engineering (oncall: eng-private-deployments-team)
- Operator: Field operator or customer operator performing hands-on steps.
- Reviewer: SRE runbook reviewer for post‑operation evidence and timelines.
- Escalation path: oncall -> runtime-leads -> security (if firmware revocation or supply chain issue suspected).

Preflight checklist (must be satisfied before any patch window):
1) Customer acceptance and maintenance window confirmed in writing.
2) Telemetry baseline capture completed (see Observability section).
3) Backup snapshots completed for persistent runtime state and KV caches where applicable.
4) Model artifact and runtime image provenance verified (signed hashes, attestation).
5) Rollback artifacts produced and staged (firmware images, package repo pointer, runtime image tag).
6) Operator has access to emergency escape route (console, IPMI/iDRAC/BMC, or equivalent).

Minimal risk table (quick reference):
| Component | Risk level | Typical impact | Rollback speed estimate |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| OS kernel/packaged deps | Medium | service restart, glibc ABI regressions rare | 15–45m per node |
| Accelerator firmware | High | degraded performance or hardware unavailability | 30–120m per node (depends on vendor tools) |
| Inference runtime library | Medium–High | model-serving failures or quantization mismatches | 10–60m per node |

Staged procedure (operator runbook):
1. Preflight verification (parallelizable):
   - Confirm customer maintenance window and SLO exceptions.
   - Snapshot runtime state: run snapshot script: 
     curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" https://localhost:5600/api/v1/operator/snapshot > /tmp/runtime-snapshot-$(date -I).json
   - Record baseline telemetry (30 minutes of representative traffic): export metrics to archive: 
     prometheus-cli snapshot --range=30m --out=/tmp/telemetry-baseline-$(date -I).tar.gz

2. Canary node update (single zone, 1 node of smallest footprint):
   - Drain ingress: mark node Unschedulable and wait for in-flight KV/cache flush.
   - Apply OS package updates using the curated repo + APT/YUM wrapper: 
     /opt/redwood/bin/apply-packages --repo=https://repo.redwood.local/private/patches/2026-02 --dry-run=false
   - If accelerating firmware: push firmware via vendor tool with attach logs to evidence bundle. Example vendor command (pseudo): fwupdater --host $BMC --image fw-2026.02.bin --verify-sig --apply
   - Restart runtime process and verify health endpoints: curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || rollback-step
   - Run post-canary smoke tests (see Test matrix).
   - Monitor telemetry for 30 minutes. If no regressions, continue.

3. Zone rollout (parallel within safety limits):
   - Schedule waves with a maximum of N concurrent nodes where N is set by capacity and customer SLA (default N=2 for high-risk firmware).
   - For each node in the wave: drain -> apply -> restart -> smoke test -> uncordon.
   - Maintain rolling prefix/KV cache shard consistency by staggering waves to avoid global cache thrash.

4. Runtime library swap (if required):
   - Use canary image tag and feature-gated rollout via the control-plane (image tags: redwood/runtime:stable-202602-canary)
   - Allow 5–10% traffic to canary path, observe quality/regression metrics, then progress to 25%, 50%, 100%.

Rollback triggers and immediate actions (TRIGGERS are monitored automatically where possible):
- Trigger examples:
  - Latency p95 increase > 2x baseline for > 15 minutes.
  - Error rate increase > 1% absolute or 3x relative baseline.
  - Accelerator device failing to initialize or absent from device list.
  - Model outputs failing integrity checks (tokenization mismatch, nan logits).
- Immediate actions:
  1. Pause the rollout (stop further waves).
  2. Revert control-plane image tag if runtime library caused regression.
  3. For firmware: put impacted nodes into maintenance mode and re-flash previous firmware image using staged rollback artifact.
  4. Notify customer stakeholders via templated message (see Communication templates).
  5. Open an incident record and attach snapshot evidence bundle.

Rollback procedure (firmware-focused):
1) Identify affected nodes using telemetry tags and device IDs.
2) For each node: instruct BMC to re-image or apply staged firmware image with verification flags. Example pseudo-command: 
   bmcctl --host $BMC --user $OP --apply /opt/rollback/fw-2025.11.bin --verify --force-if-unsigned
3) Validate device presence and driver handoff: dmesg | grep -i accel; redwood-admin device list --json
4) Restart runtime and run full smoke and regression test suite.
5) Preserve forensic evidence (firmware update logs, signed hashes, control-plane job ID) and attach to incident.

Observability and telemetry (what to capture):
- Mandatory metrics: request_latency_p95, request_error_rate, device_online_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_quality_regression_score.
- Logs: firmware_update_* logs, system journal, kernel oops, vendor device logs.
- Traces: distributed traces for representative requests to detect tail latency regressions.
- Evidence bundle format: 
  - /evidence/<date>/telemetry-baseline.tar.gz
  - /evidence/<date>/firmware-apply-logs.tar.gz
  - /evidence/<date>/snapshots/runtime-snapshot.json

Test matrix (smoke and verification):
1) Health endpoints: /health, /ready, runtime-admin/kv-status
2) Functional smoke: Gen small/medium/large requests and compare tokenization and top-5 logits against baseline hashes.
3) Performance smoke: 100 synthetic requests with production concurrency distribution; assert p95 < baseline*1.5
4) Device verification: run vendor diag and ensure pass status = true

SLO impact and customer communication:
- Typical maintenance window template: clear statement of expected maximum interruption (e.g., "Best effort: <5m per node; worst case: node offline up to 60m while firmware reflash completes").
- Any anticipated SLO excursions must be pre-approved; update customer SLA sheet and notify account owner.

Communication templates (short):
- Pre-window: "Redwood will perform scheduled firmware/security patching on <date> between <start> and <end>. We expect nominal impact; in the unlikely event of rollback we will follow our incident playbook and provide updates."
- On-deviation: "We have paused the rollout due to observed regression in zone <zone>. Immediate rollback is in progress. Next update in 30 minutes."
- Post-completion: "Maintenance completed. Attached evidence bundle. Please file any post-check concerns within 72 hours."

Post-operation review and evidence retention:
- Create an internal review ticket with attached evidence bundle and performance charts.
- Required fields in the review ticket: operator, start/end times, artifacts applied (package/firmware/runtime tag), telemetry diff summary, rollback occurrences and root-cause hypothesis.
- Retention: evidence bundle kept for 180 days for regulated customers (longer per contract).

Appendix A — Emergency escape actions (fastest path):
- If device-level failure prevents safe reflash, isolate node from load (force-evict) and mark as quiesced in operator console. Prepare same-day physical RMA process as described in the field hardware handbook.

Appendix B — Vendor-specific notes (examples):
- Vendor A (AccelX): requires BMC session with token renewal every 10 minutes during flash. Use accelx-fwcli --keepalive 600. Failure modes: incomplete flash leaves device in "fallback" mode; manual force-recovery required.
- Vendor B (MatrixAccel): supports A/B firmware partitions; rollback is quick but needs driver handshake. Always wait for driver-bound metric before uncordon.
